correspondence.finding: The selected northwestern opening lies beside a small pond in the mapped Swift Creek valley south of the major east–west road. The succeeding eastward and southeastward bends remain in that same named creek corridor through the gently rolling, partly settled headward terrain. This is a selected start, not a verified natural source.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The creek continues southeast past the Turkey Creek tributary setting and into the northwestern arm of Swift Creek Reservoir. The mapped blue stream and widening impounded valley establish the ordinary entering connection.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The three successive parts cross the mapped open-water reservoir from its northern/western entering arms to its southeastern outlet setting. The cartography distinctly labels Swift Creek Reservoir, with other creek arms joining from the sides. An exact wetted river thread within the impoundment is neither necessary nor claimed.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selection leaves the southeastern reservoir end and follows the mapped Swift Creek corridor eastward and southeastward through road crossings and tributary entries. The reservoir outlet and downstream corridor are connected in the map; nearby side valleys are not substituted for the selected route.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The long stored part first proceeds east in the clearly labeled Swift Creek valley, then turns south through the more sinuous wooded creek corridor. Its generalized straight segments remain within the same connected valley and receiving floor despite finer mapped bends.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower swift and falling creek junction
correspondence.finding: The creek continues southeast below the Falling Creek junction setting and along the widening lower valley. Mapped channel, adjacent lowland and tributary entries support the entire interval through to the next eastward turn.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower swift colonial heights and appomattox join
correspondence.finding: The selected route follows lower Swift Creek eastward through the Colonial Heights setting, including impounded/widened water and road crossings, then reaches the larger Appomattox receiving corridor. The two river names are kept separate; a precise hydronym-transition vertex is not asserted.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The short part and following northeastward bends occupy the clearly labeled Appomattox River and its adjoining swampy floodplain. The continuous receiving corridor extends past the McLaughlin and point-of-rocks setting toward the highway crossing. Side creeks and parallel wetland channels do not create an unresolved transfer.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selection continues east along the broad lower Appomattox beside Hopewell. Repeated river labels, continuous water and bordering tidal lowland establish the passage toward the James River junction.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The final part continues through the confluence-side Appomattox mouth setting into the James River receiving margin. The source endpoint and the slightly more southwestern rendered endpoint were considered separately; both occupy this same broad inland tidal-river junction setting. The stored sea-class terminal does not establish an ocean mouth, and neither endpoint is claimed as an exact surveyed bank or legal river boundary.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selected opening occupies the broad Nehalem valley near the northeastern tributary and road setting. It follows the valley southwest and then south to the highway crossing, where Nehalem River is directly labeled. Generalized segments cross portions of the same alluvial floor rather than requiring an exact modern meander match; no natural-source claim is made.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: Below the highway the chosen corridor turns west and reaches the Humbug Creek receiving setting. Mapped river and enclosing slopes establish the westgoing turn without substituting the incoming northern creek.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lost lake and spruce run reaches
correspondence.finding: The river proceeds south through the Lost Lake Creek setting, then southwest and west past Spruce Run Creek. Successive bends and the directly labeled Nehalem corridor remain connected within the same constrained valley; both side creeks retain tributary scope.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selected southward bends pass the Cronin Creek junction and continue through the enclosing canyon. The generalized path stays in the same low river trough despite omitting several mapped meanders.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The corridor turns west through the Salmonberry River tributary setting and follows the broad westgoing Nehalem valley beside the transport corridor. The map repeatedly names Nehalem River; the southern tributary is not used as an alternative path or whole-selection name.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The river makes its pronounced southward bend past the Lost Creek and McDonald Creek settings, arriving at the fragment boundary within the same valley. correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The next fragment continues west through the same Nehalem valley and its short north–south bends. Mapped river water, the adjoining valley floor and hills establish passage past the small tributary entries toward the lower settled valley.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selected route passes the Foley Creek tributary setting and turns north through the large lower river loop. correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: north fork join and lower estuary
correspondence.finding: The route reaches the North Fork Nehalem River confluence-side setting, then turns southwest and south through the low estuarine river plain. The North Fork and local sloughs are bounded components; no single present-flow branch is inferred for every generalized position.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selection extends west into the clearly labeled Nehalem Bay and turns south through the same open estuarine waterbody behind the coastal spit. Continuous receiving water establishes the bay passage without needing a distinct river thread across its interior.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: bay entrance and distinct coastal endings
correspondence.finding: The final part continues down the bay toward its ocean entrance and turns near the southern end of the spit. The source endpoint lies farther south and west in the entrance-side receiving setting; the rendered endpoint is farther north and east near the spit/entrance margin. They were considered separately within the same connected bay-mouth coastal setting. Neither is claimed to fit an exact contemporary jetty tip, bank or surveyed mouth line.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selected start occupies an already established sediment-bearing river valley. correspondence.finding: The river turns southwest through a sequence of visible bends and short narrower reaches between forested slopes. Alluvial clearings broaden alongside the river. correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The final part of the first fragment turns south and then west along the broad curved alluvial floor. Entering and leaving river segments, adjoining floodplain and forested valley sides establish the same receiving corridor across the partly clouded southern bend and stored-fragment seam.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: From the shared seam the river turns northwest through broad meanders with vegetated bars and pale sediment margins. The sequence remains within one connected alluvial floor despite local cloud and the simplified rendered bends.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: A pronounced loop, its northward exit and successive west-northwest bends are visible amid forest and scattered riverside clearings. correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The route bends southwest from the middle northern turn and follows a broad sediment-bearing river past partly cloudy floodplain. It then turns west and north. correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The river becomes a broad open northgoing channel with islands and low forested banks, then bends northwest. Adjacent narrow side channels remain within the same floodplain. correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selection continues north past a branching reach and river-side settlement, retaining the broader northgoing river rather than the separate westgoing arm. An island divides the visible flow locally. The low wooded floodplain connects all selected segments.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The route continues north and then west through the lower branch network. correspondence.finding: The westgoing branch widens toward the coast and divides around vegetated islands. No claim is made that it follows one exact modern wet thread.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The last part crosses the mouth-side island/channel transition. correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selected beginning lies within the northern part of a built-up settlement on the broad valley floor. Cultivated patches and coarse path offsets remain within this common valley floor; no engineered drainage operation is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: western floor and mountain front passage
correspondence.finding: The two short parts follow the north-running western margin of the same alluvial floor. The coarse selection stays beside the foot of the western fans and a long shallow drainage strip, east of cultivated circular fields. Both parts and their join are continuous at ordinary valley-floor scale; no exact present channel or banks are claimed.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: 1-based within the unchanged sole stored fragment; both span endpoints are inclusive

correspondence.component_scope: northeast sweep and central lower floor
correspondence.finding: The route bends northeast and then continues generally north through open alluvium, passing shallow swales, fan toes and branching darker drainage traces. Parts seven through nine occupy one connected valley floor. The visibly darker contemporary traces sometimes lie east or west of the generalized selection; those local offsets do not require an interbasin crossing.

The full approach, side-fan joins and entry remain visible in the clean northern crop. Dry-looking surfaces do not require an active wet thread for this correspondence.

The separately supplied source and rendered terminal metadata coincide here; both are preserved at their supplied endpoint on the southern playa interior/margin setting. They are not moved to the playa centre or a photographed water boundary. The retained endorheic class is consistent with this observed receiving-basin setting, without proving present water balance.
